label: Alternate: recycling split by stage, origin and dry matter
description: An alternate to 2025-fuel, not a later layer, and a change to the method (line 2 of the two lines of enquiry: the thesis method is kept in 2025-fuel). The thesis credits a share of ALL losses as animal feed, in wet grams. Here the recyclable losses are split as the workbook's own loss chain gives them (primary to retail, retail, consumer avoidable, inedible parts, processing), animal-origin food waste is left out (feeding it is banned by the swill rules), only feed-grade processing by-products count (whey, bran, oilseed meal, potato and corn residues; not shells, bagasse, pomace or grounds), and every gram is counted at its dry matter against a feed conversion ratio measured on dry feed. The recycling setting keeps its meaning as the uptake of what can be fed (short term 0%, long term 100%, as in the thesis). The tables are in Settings!BK1:BM40 and can be edited.

patches.reason: Short-term uptake of the feed pool that the method counts: the share of each stage's feed-grade pool that was fed in 2018-19, weighted by the size of the pool (FIAL 2021 Table 3; analysis/waste_2025/pool.csv). Retail 11%, manufacturing 56%, households, food service and procurement none; primary production is not measured and counted as none. The thesis short-term setting was 0%.

Settings.BK1: Recycling split by stage (line 2): share of each part of the recyclable losses that can be fed to animals
Settings.BK12: whey and skim milk (cheese, butter, yoghurt)
Settings.BK13: bran, germ and offal (milling, rice, oats)
Settings.BK16: shells, hulls, bagasse, pomace, grounds (not fed)
Settings.BK19: Dry matter of the food as wasted (by diet category)
Settings.BK40: Dry matter of feed (the basis of the feed conversion ratios, Recycle!E)

errata: Dry matters are medians of raw foods by diet category (AUSNUT 2007), not item by item; the feed-grade shares of by-products are judgements listed in Settings!BL12:BL17.

Processing by-products such as whey, bran and oilseed meal are already fed to animals today (food manufacturing sends 6.25 million tonnes a year to animal feed, FIAL 2021); the model prices all feed as primary crops, so the credit is not double counted, but the short-term setting of 0% understates current practice.

The shares of consumer-level and primary-to-retail plant waste that can actually be collected and fed are not measured in Australia; the method counts the legal ceiling and leaves the uptake to the recycling setting.
